author: Chris Talley
title: Texas to surpass California in battery storage, Permian Basin to benefit - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Talley ,
6 hours ago
ODESSA, Texas (KMID/KPEJ) – Texas is constantly growing. Since 2021 more than 2.1 million residents moved to the Lone Star State, adding to the need for power grid reliability.
“[Texas] is growing at, maybe double, the rate of California and probably most of the rest of the country. When you grow at that rate, you put significant demand on the grid and the infrastructure that’s in place. You’re connecting more load to that infrastructure, and it just doesn’t have the capacity,” explained Jon Williams, CEO, Veridi – a company that develops failsafe lithium-ion battery energy storage systems .
While Texas is expected to see an additional 4.4 million residents added to the population by 2050, even more energy output will be needed across the state.
“Battery storage is a key component of any energy management design. It has not been that way traditionally, but it is increasingly and very quickly becoming that way,” said Williams.
Williams said how the future of battery storage could help add to the Permian Basin’s energy production.
“Batteries allow all these assets that we have in our economy today, and that are powered by the Permian Basin, not only to run more efficiently, but to basically do more for us. We get more output from that same unit of energy,” explained Williams.
A recent study by the Solar Energy Industries Association shows Texas is set to surpass California’s battery storage — as a record breaking 57.6 gigawatt hours were reached in 2025.
Williams discussed why having batteries could be the new standard for the electric grid — rather than something considered as a back-up commodity.
“[Energy consumers] can’t continue to rely on an electrical system that doesn’t have battery backup. The challenge with our electrical system today is that it’s an on-demand system, so the minute there’s a problem at the generation, at the transmission, at the distribution, or at the delivery – we lose power, but if [energy providers] put battery storage behind the meter, things like a generator can go down and you won’t lose power,” explained Williams.
